hypothesis: Non-financial HS300 firms that simultaneously rank well on management-cost discipline, operating cash-flow conversion and gross-margin improvement should earn higher future returns than firms where a strong component compensates for weakness in another.
selection_basis: R232's equal-weight SG&A + OCF-margin + gross-margin-trend composite passed its recent-year and cost-stress checks but failed the discovery-set relative-return gate; R241 later found its contribution concentrated in a few names. Before preregistration, two min-rank variants using SG&A were rejected because the SG&A component has only 98.4557% coverage, below the frozen 99% gate; evidence: r252_minrank_rejected.json. Replacing SG&A with the management-expense component yields 100% joint coverage and a maximum mean absolute correlation of 0.447280 with the audited existing-factor set; evidence: r253_data_feasibility.json. No forward returns for the new factor were read.

factor.formula: management_ocf_gm_min_rank = min(rank_pct(management_expense_ratio_4q_low), rank_pct(ocf_margin_4q), rank_pct(gross_margin_yoy_improvement_q)); each rank_pct is a same-date cross-sectional percentile within the current non-financial historical HS300 membership, with 1 = best and 0 = worst
factor.interpretation: Higher means the firm's weakest of cost discipline, cash conversion and gross-margin direction is still strong relative to peers.
factor.pit_rule: Each component inherits its existing financial PIT effective date. The min-rank is computed only from same-date component values and historical HS300 membership; no future financial report, future return, or full-sample rank is used.
factor.missing_data_rule: Require all three components to be non-null. Missing components remain null; no partial score, zero fill, interpolation, cross-sectional fallback or industry mean substitution.
factor.universe: historical HS300 membership excluding banks and non-bank financials using the current industry snapshot

strategies.weight_rationale: The min-rank receives the fixed 45% research weight used in recent rounds. The remaining quality and cash weights preserve the 54.5/45.5 ratio of the matched control. No weight was selected using forward returns.
strategies.matched_requirements: Both strategies use the same non-financial HS300 universe, three-component availability filter, 30-name score limit, top 10 equal-weight positions, 20-day holding period, -20% stop loss, T+1 open execution and cost model.

execution.cost_stress: 4x and 5x scale all four cost components proportionally

segments.stitching: compound two independently run segment curves; skip the first return of each later segment

factor_ic.method: month-end factor value versus T+1 open to T+21 open forward return within historical non-financial HS300 members; cross-sectional Spearman rank IC

gates.D1: full-period non-financial member-row factor coverage from 2023-05-04 onward >= 0.99
gates.D3: same-date min-rank construction, component coverage, ties, historical membership and PIT audit pass
gates.D4: maximum mean absolute monthly rank correlation with the preregistered existing-factor set <= 0.70
gates.I1: discovery mean rank IC >= 0.02 with at least 18 month-end observations
gates.I2: validation mean rank IC >= 0.01 with at least 18 month-end observations and the same positive sign
gates.G2: discovery candidate MDD is no worse than control MDD by more than 5pp
gates.G4: full-sample candidate return > 0 and >= control return
gates.G5: full-sample candidate MDD <= 40% in absolute value and no worse than control by more than 5pp
gates.G6: rolling 1-year positive rate >= 60% and no worse than control by more than 2pp
gates.G7: recent 12-month candidate return > 0 and MDD no worse than control by more than 5pp
gates.G8: full-sample candidate return at 4x cost is positive
gates.G9: full-sample candidate return at 5x cost is positive
gates.C1: at least 30 distinct symbols are traded across the full sample
gates.C2: the largest symbol's share of net P&L is <= 25%
gates.C3: the top three symbols' share of net P&L is <= 55%
gates.C4: the top five symbols' share of net P&L is <= 75%
gates.C5: at least 8 distinct symbols have positive P&L in the validation segment
gates.C6: the largest industry's share of gross profit is <= 45%
gates.C7: the largest single-symbol loss is <= 20% of gross profit in absolute value

decision_rule: All D, I, G and C gates must pass. Any failure means the factor is not accepted and cannot be rescued by changing the min-rank rule, management-cost component, weights, holding period, stop loss, universe, costs or gates after seeing results.
known_limitations: The weakest-link rule can make the factor sparse when a strong component is paired with a weak component.
Average percentile ranks can produce ties, including a 1st-percentile value of zero.
Management expenses do not capture selling expenses and may be classified inconsistently across firms.
All components use current financial snapshots and inherit restatement risk.
The industry snapshot used to exclude financials is current rather than historical PIT.
This is another composite built from the same broad quality-factor family, so multiple-comparison risk remains.
Passing these gates would justify further paper-trading validation, not production deployment.
